title: CPU, GPU, Accelerators, and Workloads
summary: Compare workload requirements with general-purpose and parallel compute resources.
objectives: Distinguish CPU and GPU workload patterns.
Compare compute, memory, storage, and network requirements.

vocab.def: General-purpose processing hardware suited to many kinds of sequential and mixed tasks.
Highly parallel processing hardware useful for graphics, scientific, and some AI workloads.
The amount of work or data handled in a period of time.

sections.heading: Match the resource to the work
sections.body: CPUs provide flexible general-purpose processing. GPUs and other accelerators can perform many parallel operations efficiently. A GPU is not only for AI, and a workload may need CPU, memory, storage, and network resources together.

sections.heading: Compare requirements
sections.body: Workloads differ in compute demand, memory, storage, bandwidth, latency, throughput, and availability. Use evidence rather than assuming one architecture fits every task.

practice.prompt: A workload has high parallel computation but also needs a large data feed. What should be compared?
practice.answer: Accelerator capacity plus memory, storage throughput, and network data movement.

quiz.question: Which statement is accurate?
options: CPUs are general purpose and GPUs can support parallel workloads
Every workload needs the same resource mix
quiz.answer: CPUs are general purpose and GPUs can support parallel workloads

criteria: Distinguishes CPU and GPU roles appropriately
Includes memory, storage, and network needs

lab.objective: Compare a synthetic workload with infrastructure resources.

reflectionPrompt: Which requirement would you verify before choosing compute hardware?
